A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe the same RISE research. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original radar experiments on layout reconstruction and object detection, including quantitative comparisons, trajectory-length sensitivity, and component ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 7–9.

M1.justification: The BAME processing, multipath inversion, hierarchical diffusion, and spatial-consistency optimization are unchanged. Section 4 and the appendix algorithm retain the same procedures and components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RISE-Indoor coverage: approximately 100 trajectories, 50,000 frames, and 11 environments for layout reconstruction and object detection. The 35,000-floor-plan simulation corpus is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BRL and EMT + SRHD as object-detection comparators. The layout comparisons retain EMT in Figures 7–9; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Acquisition and preprocessing procedures, 30-second trajectories, shorter-trajectory evaluations, and Chamfer distance, F1 at 15 cm, IoU, and Dice metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3, 5, and 8.

E4.justification: The trajectory-length sensitivity analysis in Figure 9, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative reconstruction examples in Figure 8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same averages and per-trajectory plots. Neither adds or changes repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. Table 1 still reports RISE IoU 57.78% and Dice 69.34%, versus EMT + SRHD at 7.70% and 12.66%. Section 5.3's 16.03 cm Chamfer value and Table 2's 16.32 cm full-model value are both unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their mathematical reasoning are unchanged, including the bi-angular formulation and appendix derivations for first- and second-bounce reflector estimation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, method, novelty, and performance claims for single-static-radar layout reconstruction and object detection.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Appendix Section 10 retains the same limitations concerning dependence on human motion, remaining blind regions, and 2D rather than full 3D outputs.

D1.justification: v3 removes the abstract's website/code availability statement and project link without replacement elsewhere, including the appendices. Other technical details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference 86 changes the title wording from '4d perception' to 'vggt-4d perception' while retaining the same authors and arXiv identifier; this is a bibliographic metadata edit.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to deleting the abstract's access sentence, updating Reference 86's title, and changing the version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization, including the appendices, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract deletion causes minor line wrapping and text reflow across pages 1–3. Reference wrapping and two citation back-reference page numbers also change. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–2 retain their content, captions, and structure.

improvement.justification: v3 removes the paper's only explicit website/code access statement and link, modestly reducing information that helps readers locate the implementation. Scientific content and appendices remain unchanged, while the reference-title update and minor reflow offer little compensating benefit. This judgment concerns documented access, not whether the code was actually withdrawn.
